 Creating a column that incrementally increases as another column increases
    Lauren Pincus <lpi...@gmail.com> Feb 12 06:07PM -0800  

    Hey D-RUG,
     
    Sorry for the awkward email subject line. I can't seem to figure out how to
    do this and don't really know what to call what I am trying to do either...
     
     
    I have one column of numbers (colA) ranging from 1.56 to 1200. I want to
    create a second column (colB) that incrementally increases as colA
    incrementally increases.
     
     
    As colA increases by 10, colB increases by 2. But this should only happen
    after values in colA reach 20. Before that colB equals 2.
     
     
    So,
     
     
    1.56 <= colA <=20, then colB == 2
     
    20 < colA<= 30, then colB == 4
     
    30 < colA <= 40, then colB == 6
     
    40 < colA <=50, then colB == 8
     
     
    ...all the way up to 1200 where colB should equal 238 (I believe)
     
     
     
    Does anyone have any bright ideas as to how to make this happen? Perhaps a
    creative function using a for loop? Thanks for any thoughts that exist out
    there!
     
     
     
    Lauren

    Noam Ross <noam...@gmail.com> Feb 12 06:33PM -0800  

    Sorry, pressed send before i meant too. Here's a quick solution:
     
    pincus = function(A) {
    if (A < 20) {
    return(2)
    } else {
    return 2*((A - 2e-10) %/% 10)
    }
    }
     
    B = pincus(A)
     
    The %/% operator does integer division, so that it returns the largest
    integer multiple of 10 that is less than (A - 2e-10). I subtract 2e-10 from
    A so this increments B only when A is slightly more than a multiple of 10.
     
     

     

    Michael Hannon <jmhannon...@gmail.com> Feb 12 07:06PM -0800  

    I think you need to do something like:
     
    colB <- sapply(colA, pincus)
     
    You can also use the "findInterval" function to do the same thing (with the
    appropriate fiddling with the intervals, similar to pincus).
     
     
     

     

    Noam Ross <noam...@gmail.com> Feb 13 03:13PM -0800  

    Michael's right. Here's a properly vectorized version that doesn't require
    sapply, and a test:
     
    pincus = function(A) {
    ifelse(test = A < 20, yes = 2, no = 2*((A - 2e-10) %/% 10))
    }
    dat = data.frame(A = c(1.56, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40, 45, 50, 1200))
    dat$B = pincus(dat$A)
     
    print(dat)
     
    ifelse is a vectorized version of if() {} else {} so it tests each value.
    With this, you get:
     
    A B
    1 1.56 2
    2 10.00 2
    3 15.00 2
    4 20.00 2
    5 30.00 4
    6 35.00 6
    7 40.00 6
    8 45.00 8
    9 50.00 8
    10 1200.00 238
